english: Let $E$ be the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{18}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{8}=1$ and let $L$ be the polar of the point $Q(3,1)$ with respect to $E$. Let $(\alpha,\beta)$ be the point of $L$ whose chord of contact with respect to $E$ has $Q$ as its midpoint. Then the value of $\alpha+\beta$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $E$ दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{18}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{8}=1$ है तथा $E$ के सापेक्ष बिन्दु $Q(3,1)$ की ध्रुवीय रेखा $L$ है। माना $L$ का वह बिन्दु $(\alpha,\beta)$ है जिसकी $E$ के सापेक्ष स्पर्श जीवा का मध्यबिन्दु $Q$ है। तब $\alpha+\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Chord of contact of $(\alpha,\beta)$: $\dfrac{\alpha x}{18}+\dfrac{\beta y}{8}=1$; matching with $\dfrac{8}{5}\cdot\dfrac{x}{6}+\dfrac{8}{5}\cdot\dfrac{y}{8}=1$: $\alpha=\dfrac{24}{5}$, $\beta=\dfrac85$
$(\alpha,\beta)$ is on $L$: $\dfrac{96}{5}+\dfrac{24}{5}=24$ (La Hire: $Q$ is on its polar), so it is the required point
solution_full: $Q(3,1)$ is inside $E$ since $\dfrac{9}{18}+\dfrac{1}{8}=\dfrac58<1$. Its polar is $T(Q)=0$: $\dfrac{3x}{18}+\dfrac{1\cdot y}{8}=1$, i.e. $L:\ 4x+3y=24$, a line lying outside $E$.
For a point $R(\alpha,\beta)$ outside $E$, the chord of contact is its polar $\dfrac{\alpha x}{18}+\dfrac{\beta y}{8}=1$.
The chord of $E$ with midpoint $Q$ is $T=S_1$: $\dfrac{3x}{18}+\dfrac{y}{8}=\dfrac{9}{18}+\dfrac{1}{8}=\dfrac58$, i.e. $\dfrac{8}{5}\cdot\dfrac{3x}{18}+\dfrac{8}{5}\cdot\dfrac{y}{8}=1$.
The chord of contact of $R$ is this chord iff $\dfrac{\alpha}{18}=\dfrac{8}{5}\cdot\dfrac{3}{18}$ and $\dfrac{\beta}{8}=\dfrac85\cdot\dfrac18$, i.e. $R=\dfrac85Q=\left(\dfrac{24}{5},\dfrac85\right)$.

$R$ lies on $L$: $4\cdot\dfrac{24}{5}+3\cdot\dfrac85=\dfrac{120}{5}=24$. This is no accident: the chord of contact of $R$ passes through $Q$, so by the pole-polar reciprocity $R$ lies on the polar of $Q$. $R$ is outside $E$ ($\dfrac{576/25}{18}+\dfrac{64/25}{8}=\dfrac{8}{5}>1$), so its chord of contact exists.
originality_note: New: among the points of the polar of an interior point Q (all of whose chords of contact pass through Q), the one whose chord of contact is bisected at Q is the pole of the T = S1 chord, R = Q/S(Q) (way 3, a family with two conditions). Closest known: chords of contact of points on a line pass through the pole of the line. Different because: the question selects one member of that family by a midpoint condition, which needs the chord of contact, the polar and T = S1 together.
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, point and curve introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked that Q is inside (so its polar is outside and every point of L is external), that R is unique, and that R lies on L. Changed: No change.
key_step: Identify the chord of contact of R with the chord T = S1 bisected at Q, giving R = (8/5)Q, and confirm R lies on the polar of Q.
justification: Two linked ideas (polar of an interior point and its reciprocity with chords of contact, plus the midpoint-chord equation), numerical answer. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q13 (L4) in using a polar-type line, but much shorter; nearest in demand to 2023-P1-Q2 (L3).

concept_use.Chord of contact for Ellipse: The point R(alpha, beta) is chosen so that its chord of contact alpha x/18 + beta y/8 = 1 is the chord bisected at Q; matching coefficients gives R = (24/5, 8/5).
concept_use.Pole and polar for Ellipse: L is the polar 4x + 3y = 24 of the interior point Q(3,1); by pole-polar reciprocity R lies on L because its chord of contact passes through Q.
